author: opt-B1

contract.sync_assumed: caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage by a block barrier
contract.sync_performed: __syncthreads inside: 2 per radix pass plus 1 init, plus 1 in the tie phase when the candidates at the k-th key exceed the remaining k
contract.n_range: N = 256 x IPT, IPT 1 to 64 under prefer_smaller_index (the tie decision is a 64-bit mask per thread), measured 1024 and 4096
contract.type_constraints: fp32 and bf16 through the radix traits, int32 indices derived from the striped tile position
contract.nan_behavior: NaN twiddles to the largest radix key and is selected first, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 is normalized to +0.0 once in the prologue so both zeros form one tie class
contract.tie_break_support: inherent under prefer_smaller_index: warp-redundant rank (knowledge base 4.5 approach C) over the exact ties after the last pass, index order on striped tiles, taken ties written at total_selected + rank without an atomic. Measured plus 19 to 51 percent latency against B1_idx not_guaranteed in this build, see findings
contract.sorted_output_support: not supported inherently, post-sort of k

correctness_notes: 14 prefer_smaller_index cells at N 1024 and 4096, 13 oracle cases each including signed_zero (2k zeros of both signs, exact index set), all passed. The 8 cells at N 32768 are unsupported (IPT 128 exceeds the 64-bit tie mask). Control is B1_idx under not_guaranteed in the same lock section (harness 0.3 --control-req).

low_level: The deterministic path adds the prologue normalization (one compare and one select per item), a tie phase that runs only when the exact ties exceed the remaining k (IPT ballots, IPT predicated table stores, one barrier, 8 table loads per owned slot, a 5-step shuffle scan, IPT base shuffles and popcs), and an epilogue whose selected-class atomic has a constant counter address. Registers 40 against 32 at IPT 4 (throughput occupancy 6 against 8), 64 against 47 at IPT 16, SASS 1304 against 992 (fp32 N 1024), 2 more BAR.SYNC (the tie barrier, warm-up and chain copy).

The structural cost is a codegen effect, not the tie phase: fp32 random has no ties at rank k (ties_at_k 1.0), so the tie phase never runs, yet the det kernel is 344 cycles slower at N 1024 k 16 (2138 against 1794). The SASS of its epilogue shows, per item, S2R SR_LANEID, VOTEU.ANY, FLO.U32, S2R SR_LTMASK, POPC, one predicated ATOMS.ADD, SHFL.IDX and the rank add: the compiler warp-aggregated the ticket atomic because its address (selected_offset[0]) is provably uniform and the increment constant, and the two special register reads (about 80 cycles of latency, T14) sit in the dependent chain of every item's store. The B1_idx epilogue indexes the counter by a data-dependent class and keeps the plain per-item ATOMS with no S2R in the timed region.

The tie phase itself (bf16 rows, 1.4 to 5.4 ties at rank k) costs about 70 cycles more than the structural part at N 1024 (bf16 plus 410 against fp32 plus 344 at k 16) and about 900 more at N 4096 k 64 (bf16 plus 1962 against fp32 plus 1096), the IPT table stores and base shuffles scale with IPT.
algorithmic: Measured cost of prefer_smaller_index in this build, B200 same lock section: N 1024 k 16 bf16 2177 against 1767 (plus 23 percent), fp32 2138 against 1794 (plus 19 percent), k 256 bf16 2410 against 1971, fp32 2425 against 2148, N 4096 k 64 bf16 5801 against 3839 (plus 51 percent), fp32 5684 against 4588 (plus 24 percent). Throughput minus 17 to 38 percent. The knowledge base 4.5 figure of about plus 1 percent on random data for approach C does not hold for this build until the aggregation is defeated, see the open question.

The rank is index order for free on striped tiles (slot-major then thread order is item order), which the blocked arrangement does not give, and the taken ties need no atomic because their position is total_selected plus rank.
negative: A constant counter address in a per-item ticket loop is a liability on sm_100 with nvcc 13.4: the automatic warp aggregation it triggers costs more than the atomics it saves when the sites are on the critical path. Use a data-dependent or opaque counter index.
surprises: The compiler's automatic warp-aggregated atomic is the whole story of the 19 percent at fp32: 4 x (S2R SR_LTMASK plus S2R SR_LANEID) on a dependent path cost about as much as the two 8-bit radix passes' scan phases together.
open_questions: The fix (an opaque counter index through an empty asm statement, now in approaches/B1/block_topk_b1.cuh) is implemented and not yet measured, the batch budget of this session was spent. Expected: the structural 344 cycles vanish and prefer_smaller_index costs the tie phase alone, about 70 cycles at IPT 4 on bf16 rows with ties and 0 on fp32 rows without.
IPT above 64 needs a wider tie mask (two 64-bit words, or a per-slot taken bit recomputed in the epilogue from the rank) to cover N 32768 at 256 threads.
